title: EU security laws: which apply to you and what is due when?
short: Map each legal entity and product to NIS2, DORA and the CRA, and set up one process that can report within 24 hours.
answer: Check which of your legal entities fall under NIS2 or DORA and which products under the CRA, since all three require a first report within 24 hours[^nis2][^dorarts][^cra]. Then resolve overlaps by role: DORA replaces NIS2's risk and reporting rules for financial entities[^nis2] and the CRA adds product duties, so one group can face all three.
audience: IT, security and compliance leads in EU organizations, especially in Germany

blocks.title: If you only do five things
blocks.intro: This is guidance, not legal advice.

items.title: Decide scope per legal entity and product.
items.text: NIS2 and DORA apply to entities[^nis2][^dora], the CRA to products with digital elements and their manufacturers, importers and distributors[^cra]. Record the sector and size figures you used.

items.title: Run one incident process with several clocks.
items.text: NIS2 and the CRA require an early warning within 24 hours[^nis2][^cra] and DORA an initial notification within 4 hours of classification as major[^dorarts]. Name who classifies incidents and who sends each report.

items.title: Have management sign off and take training.
items.text: Management bodies must approve and oversee the NIS2 risk management measures and take training, and they can be held liable[^nis2]. Put both on the board calendar.

items.title: Map your controls to the NIS2 measures.
items.text: Article 21 requires measures in at least ten areas, from incident handling and backups to supply chain security and multi-factor authentication[^nis2]. Give each gap an owner and a date.

items.title: Put the duties into supplier contracts.
items.text: DORA requires a register of information on all ICT service contracts[^dora] and NIS2 requires supply chain security[^nis2]. Add security update, incident notification and audit clauses at renewal.

blocks.title: Find out which laws apply to you

items.title: Do you supply connected products in the EU?
items.text: If you make, import or distribute hardware or software that connects to a device or network, the CRA applies to those products[^cra]. Medical devices, motor vehicles and certified aviation products are excluded, as are cloud services that aren't remote data processing for a product[^cra].

items.title: Are you a financial entity under DORA?
items.text: DORA lists 20 types, including credit institutions, payment and e-money institutions, investment firms, crypto-asset service providers, insurers and fund managers[^dora]. For them it replaces NIS2's risk management, reporting and supervision[^nis2].

items.title: Is your sector in NIS2 Annex I or II?
items.text: NIS2 covers 18 sectors, among them energy, transport, health, finance, digital infrastructure, digital services, critical product manufacturing, waste, postal services and public administration[^ecnis2]. If no annex lists your type of entity, NIS2 generally doesn't apply[^nis2].

items.title: How big is the entity?
items.text: An Annex I or II entity is in scope with 50 or more employees, or with turnover and balance sheet both above €10 million. An Annex I entity is essential with 250 or more employees, or with turnover above €50 million and a balance sheet above €43 million[^sme][^nis2]. Telecom, trust service and DNS providers and TLD registries are in scope at any size[^nis2].

blocks.title: The three laws side by side

columns.title: NIS2
items: **Who.** Medium and large entities in the Annex I and II sectors, plus telecom, trust service and DNS providers and TLD registries at any size[^nis2].
**Duties.** Management-approved risk management measures in at least ten areas, incident reporting and registration with the national authority[^nis2].
**Dates.** Member States had to apply it from 18 October 2024[^nis2].

**Penalties.** Maximum fines of at least €10 million or 2% of worldwide turnover, whichever is higher, for essential entities and €7 million or 1.4% for important ones[^nis2]. Managers of essential entities can be temporarily barred[^nis2].

columns.title: DORA
items: **Who.** 20 types of financial entity[^dora], plus critical ICT providers: 19 designated in November 2025, including AWS, Microsoft and SAP[^ctpp].

**Duties.** An ICT risk management framework owned by the management body, major incident reporting, resilience testing and a register of information on all ICT service contracts[^dora]. Threat-led penetration tests at least every 3 years for entities their supervisor selects[^dora].
**Dates.** Applies since 17 January 2025[^dora].
**Penalties.** Set by Member States, also for management body members[^dora]. Daily penalties of up to 1% of average daily worldwide turnover for critical ICT providers[^dora].

columns.title: CRA
items: **Who.** Manufacturers, importers and distributors of connected hardware and software in the EU[^cra].
**Duties.** The Annex I security requirements, a software bill of materials, CE marking and vulnerability handling for a support period of at least 5 years, or the expected use time if shorter[^cra].
**Dates.** In force since 10 December 2024[^eccra]. Reporting applies from 11 September 2026 and the remaining duties from 11 December 2027[^cra].
**Penalties.** Up to €15 million or 2.5% of worldwide turnover for breaches of Annex I or Articles 13 and 14[^cra].

blocks.title: What you can skip
items: **Waiting for the proposed changes.** Neither the reporting rules in the general Digital Omnibus nor the NIS2 amendments are law yet[^council][^oeil], and the proposed single entry point would keep today's reporting duties and recipients[^ecdigital].
**A separate compliance program for each law.** Keep one risk register for all three and add law-specific steps only where the duties differ.

**Reporting every alert.** NIS2 requires reports only for incidents that cause or could cause severe operational disruption, financial loss or considerable damage to others[^nis2]. Give the on-call team written thresholds.

blocks.title: Mistakes that cost the most
items: **Leaving group companies out of the size test.** The EU test adds the figures of linked and partner enterprises[^sme].
**Waiting for the full picture to report.** The NIS2 early warning only has to say whether you suspect unlawful or malicious acts or cross-border impact[^nis2].
**Forgetting products already on the market.** CRA reporting also covers products placed on the market before December 2027[^cra].
**Missing the implementing regulation.** Cloud, data center, managed service and other digital providers must also meet the detailed requirements of Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2690[^nis2ir].

blocks.title: Reporting clocks
blocks.intro: Each clock starts when you become aware, unless noted.

items.name: NIS2
items.scope: Significant incidents, to the CSIRT or competent authority; in Germany, the BSI[^bsig]. The final report is due 1 month after the notification[^nis2].

items.name: DORA
items.scope: Major ICT-related incidents, to the competent authority. The 4 hours run from classification, capped at 24 hours after awareness unless you classify later; later clocks run from the previous report[^dorarts].

items.name: CRA
items.scope: Manufacturers, through ENISA's platform[^enisa]. The final report is due 14 days after a fix for actively exploited vulnerabilities and 1 month after the notification for severe incidents[^cra].

blocks.title: Germany: the NIS2 Implementation Act
items: **The law took effect on 6 December 2025.** The act was published in the Bundesgesetzblatt on 5 December 2025, with no general transition period[^bgbl][^bsifaq]. It applies to about 29,500 companies and federal institutions[^bsiportal].

**The registration deadline has passed.** Entities must register within 3 months of falling under the law, so the first deadline passed in March 2026[^bsig][^bsinis2]. If you haven't registered, get an ELSTER organization certificate through Mein Unternehmenskonto, then register in the BSI portal[^bsinis2], open since 6 January 2026[^bsiportal]. Report changes within 2 weeks[^bsig].

**DORA entities must register too.** They are exempt from the BSIG's risk management, reporting and management body duties, and the BSIG rules out reporting the same incident under both laws[^bsifaq].
**Group figures can be left out.** The BSIG excludes linked and partner enterprises from the size test if your IT systems run independently of theirs[^bsig].
**Management is liable to the entity.** It must implement and oversee the risk management measures and attend regular training, and it is liable for culpable damage under company law[^bsig].

blocks.title: What changed in 2026
items: **CRA reporting started.** Since 11 September 2026 manufacturers must report actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe incidents[^cra].

**The Commission proposed NIS2 amendments.** Its proposal of 20 January 2026 would clarify the scope to ease compliance for 28,700 companies, add a small mid-cap category and simplify jurisdiction rules[^ecqa]. It still awaits a committee decision in Parliament[^oeil].

**The Council wants national reporting entry points.** The general Digital Omnibus, separate from the one on AI, would let you file NIS2, DORA, GDPR and other reports through one ENISA entry point[^ecdigital]. The Council's position of 21 October 2026 swaps it for one national entry point per Member State and backs a longer GDPR breach deadline; Parliament has not adopted its position yet[^council].

changes.text: Clarified that the general Digital Omnibus, still a proposal, is separate from the Digital Omnibus on AI, which is in force.
